name: ZEBRA (Zero Extrinsic Back Ratio) - Call
summary: Buy 2 deep ITM calls and sell 1 ATM call; a three-contract package with roughly 100 deltas and essentially zero net extrinsic value, used as a defined-risk stock replacement.

legs.strike_rule: ATM strike, call delta 0.48-0.52 (covered by the 2 longs)

when_to_use: When a bullish directional view is wanted with about 100 deltas but far less capital than 100 shares and no theta bleed. The extrinsic paid on the 2 longs is approximately offset by the extrinsic sold on the 1 short, so time decay is near zero - the defining property.
max_profit: UNLIMITED (behaves like 100 long shares above the ATM strike)
max_loss: net debit paid. Defined - this is the main advantage over actual shares.
breakevens: approximately the ATM strike plus (net debit/100) minus the intrinsic already embedded; in practice close to spot at entry

greeks.delta: approximately +100 per unit at entry (2 x 0.72 - 0.50 = 0.94, scaled by 100)
greeks.theta: near zero by construction - the whole point of the structure

entry_rules: Long strike delta between 0.70 and 0.75; short strike delta between 0.48 and 0.52.
Net extrinsic check: (2 x long extrinsic) - (1 x short extrinsic) must be <= $0.15 per share; reject the fill otherwise - if it is not near-zero-extrinsic it is not a ZEBRA.
Net delta between 0.90 and 1.05 per unit.
Debit (the max loss) <= 3% of equity per unit.
30-60 DTE; avoid weeklies where the ITM strikes are illiquid.
Both strikes: OI >= 500, per-leg spread <= max($0.10, 10% of mid) - ITM strikes are wider, so the threshold is loosened.
Single 3-contract multi-leg order at mid, pay up to mid + $0.05.
management_rules: Manage it like a stock position: take profit at a defined price target or a trailing stop, not at a percentage of premium.
Default profit target: close when the package gains 50% of the debit paid; default stop: close at 35% loss of the debit.
Roll out at 14 DTE to keep the near-zero-theta property; ITM extrinsic collapses in the final two weeks and the short leg's assignment risk rises.
Re-strike if the underlying moves so far that the long delta exceeds 0.90 (the structure has become 200 deltas).
exit_rules: ASSIGNMENT GUARD: 1 short ATM call, covered by 2 long ITM calls. Flatten by 15:45 ET on expiration day, unconditionally.
ASSIGNMENT GUARD: close immediately if the short call is ITM with extrinsic < $0.10 - which happens routinely because the whole structure is built on near-zero extrinsic.
DIVIDEND GUARD: this structure is unusually exposed - ITM/ATM calls with near-zero extrinsic are the classic early-assignment target. Close or roll the entire package before every ex-dividend date.
assignment_risk: Elevated relative to its simple appearance. The short ATM call carries minimal extrinsic by design, which is precisely the condition that triggers early exercise, especially ahead of dividends. Assignment delivers -100 shares hedged by 2 long ITM calls; the economics hold, but the system ends up short stock. Roll ahead of ex-dividend dates as a rule, not an exception.
buying_power: Net debit paid only; the 2 longs cover the 1 short.
liquidity_needs: Moderate; deep ITM strikes have wider spreads and thinner open interest, so restrict to SPY, QQQ, IWM and mega-caps.
common_mistakes: Picking strikes without verifying the near-zero net extrinsic condition (turning it into an expensive ratio); holding into the final two weeks where the property breaks down; ignoring dividend assignment on the short leg.
zero_dte_notes: Not applicable - deep ITM 0DTE options have no extrinsic to balance and the assignment risk is immediate.
family: three-leg-structures (butterflies, broken-wing butterflies, lizards, three-strike ratio spreads, ladders/tree spreads, christmas trees, and three-leg stock+option hybrids)
